security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced examples, ordinary email text, and the word "understand"; no Ruby backtick execution or reconnaissance is present. Two external-command findings are confirmed because the rollback guidance recommends destructive Git commands that can erase unrelated uncommitted work. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or net-new semantic security issue was found.

remediation.issue: Rollback guidance uses destructive Git commands that can remove unrelated work.
remediation.suggestion: Replace hard reset and checkout advice with patch-based reversal or a temporary branch, and require explicit confirmation before discarding changes.

content.user_title: Fix Python Formatting and Lint Issues
content.value_statement: Formatting and lint errors slow reviews and block quality gates. This skill applies Black, isort, and Ruff fixes, then verifies results.
actual_capabilities: Guides Black and isort formatting through existing project commands.
Applies Ruff automatic fixes to selected source and test paths.
Previews formatting and lint changes with check and diff modes.
Resolves common long-line and formatter conflicts using focused refactoring patterns.
Verifies changes with project checks and reports modified files and outcomes.
limitations: Requires the project to install and configure Black, isort, Ruff, and relevant make targets.
Does not repair business logic, failing tests, complex type annotations, or missing documentation.
Provides workflow instructions but does not include the referenced automation scripts.
Automatic fixes and rollback commands can overwrite work, so users must review and checkpoint changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Python Commit
use_cases.description: Format changed files, remove safe lint violations, run checks, and review the resulting diff before committing.

use_cases.title: Address Review Feedback
use_cases.description: Apply requested formatting and lint cleanup to specific files while preserving unrelated code changes.

use_cases.title: Repair a Quality Gate
use_cases.description: Reproduce CI formatting failures locally, apply configured fixes, and verify the complete project check.

prompt_templates.title: Fix One Python File
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix formatting and safe lint issues in [file]. Review the project configuration first, show the diff, and run relevant checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cleanup for one known file

prompt_templates.title: Preview Project Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview quality fixes for [path] without changing files. Report Black, isort, and Ruff findings grouped by file.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Formatter Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve Black and Ruff conflicts in [path]. Preserve behavior, prefer focused refactoring, and verify both tools after each change.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Quality Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply only [fix types] across [scope]. Create a recoverable checkpoint, preserve unrelated work, run tests, and summarize every modified file.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced selective cleanup across a repository

best_practices: Read project conventions and tool configuration before applying fixes.
Preview and review diffs before accepting automatic changes.
Run targeted tests and the complete quality check after editing.
anti_patterns: Do not apply every available fix without checking semantic changes.
Do not use destructive Git rollback commands on uncommitted work.
Do not assume formatter success means business logic is correct.

faq.question: Which tools does this skill use?
faq.answer: It guides workflows using Black, isort, Ruff, project make targets, tests, and Git review commands.

faq.question: Can it fix one file?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a file path and request targeted formatting, lint fixes, verification, and a diff summary.

faq.question: Can it preview changes?
faq.answer: Yes. Request dry-run mode to inspect formatter and lint results without changing files.

faq.question: Does it fix failing tests?
faq.answer: No. It runs tests for verification but does not diagnose or repair test failures.

faq.question: Does it include an automation script?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains instructions only, although its documentation references example script paths.

faq.question: How should I protect uncommitted work?
faq.answer: Review the working tree, create a recoverable checkpoint, and avoid destructive restore commands without explicit confirmation.
